claims.text: Adding a controlled amount of an alloying element can introduce lattice distortion in an as-cast eutectic high-entropy alloy.
Controlled alloying-induced lattice distortion can simultaneously increase strength and ductility.
Boron or carbon can serve as the lattice-distortion-inducing alloying addition.
Excessive lattice distortion can cause embrittlement.
Processing that produces a homogeneous distribution of the added element is required for the proposed benefit.
The alloying addition produces lattice distortion and a resulting increase in dislocation density.
The increased dislocation density raises strength through dislocation hardening.
A controlled amount of lattice distortion improves ductility by promoting twinning and other deformation mechanisms.
The intervention will increase yield strength by at least 10% relative to the as-cast alloy without the addition.
The intervention will improve elongation to failure by at least 15% relative to the as-cast alloy without the addition.
The simultaneous strength and ductility improvement occurs only within a particular range of lattice distortion.
Distortion beyond the beneficial range decreases ductility.

contradictions.description: The boundary explicitly predicts that excessive distortion will decrease ductility, but the falsification rule also treats that same observation as falsifying the hypothesis. An outcome predicted by the stated boundary cannot by itself be a decisive falsifier.
